story: The world's youngest country has never held a national election. South Sudan won independence in 2011 amid huge hope, and within two and a half years its president, Salva Kiir, a Dinka, and his deputy, Riek Machar, a Nuer, had led their communities into a civil war that killed some 400,000 people. A 2018 peace deal put them back in government together. In 2026, Machar spent the year on trial for treason, murder and terrorism, under house arrest, while the government insisted the first elections would finally happen in December (AP via Yahoo).

The charges stem from a March 2025 clash in Upper Nile that the government blamed on Machar's allies. His trial, with seven co-defendants, dragged past its 68th session, and the African Union called for his release to allow a ceasefire and dialogue (Radio Tamazuj). UN experts warned that the peace deal was eroding, that both sides' forces faced off across much of the country, and that an under-supplied army was relying on "relatively indiscriminate" air strikes, with Ugandan troops backing Kiir. The information minister vowed elections in December with "no further extension" (Arab News). Analysts say the trial's real purpose is to keep Machar out of any vote. Meanwhile, war in neighbouring Sudan has cut oil exports and sent refugees south, in a country where most people already depend on aid.
briefing.power: A transitional government under the 2018 peace agreement, sharing posts among Kiir's SPLM, Machar's SPLM-IO and other parties, with a president, five vice presidents and an expanded appointed parliament. In practice Kiir rules by decree, frequently firing officials without consultation.
briefing.holders: President Salva Kiir, in office since independence in 2011.
